title: Attention as search
summary: One head, one query: the dot products behind an attention pattern.

steps.text: Each position makes three vectors: a **query** (what am I looking for?), a **key** (what do I offer?) and a **value** (what do I pass on?). Attention compares one query with every earlier key.
steps.prompt: Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She

steps.text: In the **Q·K explorer**, the top bar strip is the query of the selected position. Each row below is an earlier key: their element-wise products, the dot product, the scaled score, and the softmax weight. Large scores come from bars that agree in sign.
Click any token in the arcs or any cell of the matrix to move the query. Then find what this head is looking at.

ask.question: In the Q·K explorer, click the key with the **largest weight** for the current query.
ask.hint: Switch the order to “by weight”: it is the top row.
ask.correct: Its score is the largest, and softmax turns the largest score into the largest weight.

steps.text: Softmax is why a modest lead in score becomes a large lead in weight: weights are `exp(score)` over the row's total. The matrix view shows every query's row at once; the masked triangle is where a query would look at the future.
